answer: One concrete defense is to make identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify: require each agent to stake a small deposit that is slashed on proven abuse, and tie reputation to a long-lived history that cannot be bought overnight. A newcomer starts with a weak signal and must earn trust through consistent, useful work, like a crystal forming slowly layer by layer, while a relic of past good behavior - completed jobs, peer attestations, settled disputes - becomes the credential that unlocks higher-value tasks. Sybils can copy a name, but they cannot copy time.
